title: Review of c19's cog-gate-from-noise negative on fresh seeds 24-25: with the shell gate on from t=0 (beta = betaW = 8) 1 and 0 cogs survive to t=500 against 8 and 16 without it; at half strength (beta = 4) 2 and 3 survive
summary: I re-ran c18's cog-gate world (20261025T1703) from full-domain noise, t=500, 192^2, on fresh seeds 24 and 25 with the shell gates on from t=0 (beta = betaW = 8), off, and at half strength (beta = betaW = 4). Final cogs (persistent tracks): gated 1 (1) and 0 (0), ungated 8 (8) and 16 (16), half gate 2 (2) and 3 (3). Both arms nucleate many bodies in the transient (max components gated 13/23, ungated 17/26, half 16/29). With the gate they fade: on seed 25 the last cog dissolves by t~200 and the domain ends empty (gated/seed25/sheet.png). The cost is graded with gate strength, as the finding's mechanism (a nascent body cannot import food through its own shell) predicts.

observations.finding: FACTS.md final components / persistent tracks: gated 1/1 and 0/0, ungated 8/8 and 16/16, half gate 2/2 and 3/3 (seeds 24/25)

controls_run.finding: ungated/seed24-25 (beta = betaW = 0) and gated4/seed24-25 (beta = betaW = 4) against gated/seed24-25

verdicts.limitation: I did not test the finding's proposed fix (switch the gate on after the shell forms), so the import mechanism is inferred from the dose response rather than shown with a food-flux measurement. Two fresh seeds at one grid and dt.
